policy.statement: Every vitest coverage exclusion is a classified, owned, expiring debt entry. An exclusion with no owner, no justification, or a passed review date is a broken gate, not a covered file.

classifications.PERMANENT_STRUCTURAL: Cannot be measured in-process (spawned-process shims, types-only modules, build output). Requires a structural reason instead of a review date.
classifications.DEAD_CODE: No production importer. Excluded because nothing ships it. Removal is mandatory, not optional.
classifications.CONTRACT_ONLY: Imported by its own contract test only. Ships a schema, not a capability; contract tests alone never certify.
classifications.SHIPPED_SURFACE: Reachable from a shipped CLI verb, release gate, or MCP tool. The v5 GA hard gate removes every entry in this class.

policy.reviewBySemantics: A passed reviewBy fails the gate. The date is a deadline to either cover the file or delete it — never a silent renewal.
policy.defectSignatureSemantics: A SHIPPED_SURFACE entry carries EITHER `defectSignatures` (regexes that MUST still match the named source file) OR a `closureState` (the asserted defect is closed and no surface of it remains) — never neither, never both. A signature is a DRIFT ALARM, not a defect prover: its job is to fire when anything about the thing the entry is about changes, so fixing code forces a ledger update in the same commit. A signature that stops matching fails the gate with 'defect closed or drifted — remove or reclassify'. This is deliberately the same mechanism as tests/corpus/detector-hashes.json: a recorded fingerprint of source that CI diffs. PERMANENT_STRUCTURAL entries are exempt — they are evidenced by a structural reason, not by a defect.
policy.shippedSurfaceCeilingMeaning: Ratchet over shipped surfaces that are not PERMANENT_STRUCTURAL, not a target. The count may fall (removal, merge, real tests) and may never rise. Structural entries are excluded from the count because they are evidenced by a structural reason rather than a removable gap.

entries.structuralReason: Spawned-process entry point. A child process's istanbul report cannot merge into the parent run, so in-process instrumentation is unmeasurable. All transport logic lives in src/mcp/transport.ts and IS ratchet-covered.
entries.justification: bug-audit G6 precedent: the same structural class as dist/**. Coverage moves to tests/contract/mcp-transport.spec.ts, which spawns the real binary.

The three asserted defects were fixed — no proposal is derived from a static finding, no zero statistics are printed, and nothing claims to have been updated — but the residual surface is exactly the guarantee, and it is the guarantee the signatures below pin so it cannot silently return.
defectSignatures: A static scan has no runtime behaviour to observe

The hardcoded zeros and the partial-ignoring GO are gone, but the report still computes its OWN GO/NO-GO rather than projecting the single determination, so the residual surface is a second verdict authority — the signature below is that refusal to grade a truncated scan, which is what a future edit would be most likely to break.
defectSignatures: A partial scan cannot support a GO verdict

entries.removalPlan: V5-001 — landed: no Playwright entries are fabricated from static findings; V5-090 — hand rendering to the reporter package.
entries.justification: Shipped as `report`. V5-001 landed twice: the suite block is always empty, and (2026-09-26) the TOP-LEVEL status is no longer derived from the findings. It used to be `partial ? "interrupted" : hasError ? "failed" : "passed"`, so a clean scan published `{status: "passed", totalTests: 0}` — a green test run over zero tests, in the first field a Playwright consumer reads. The status is now the literal `interrupted` and the scan's own outcome moved to `mjolnir.scanOutcome`. The signatures below are written against that post-fix state, which is why this task had to land after it.

entries.removalPlan: V5-006 — wire m26:audit into `certify` so the validators gate engineering certification, then cover the validator branches.
entries.justification: Runs inside the release gate via `npm run m26:audit`. A gate that is not covered is a gate that can silently stop working. The signatures are the schema the gate enforces: a required-field list that shrinks, or a record cap that grows without review, is the validator quietly accepting records it used to reject.

entries.removalPlan: V5-007 — single-source the version identity, then cover the drift-detection branches.
entries.justification: Runs inside `npm run version:check` on every certify. Version drift detection that is itself untested is exactly the class of defect this ledger exists to expose. The signatures are the drift rules themselves: dropping one of them would let a surface install a version that does not exist on the registry, and nothing else would notice.

entries.removalPlan: V5-080 — generate VERBS, help, README, and the site reference from one command manifest, which makes the entry point fully reachable by tests.
entries.justification: The shipped entry point. Every verb registration is a branch; a generated command manifest (V5-080) is what lifts it above the floor. The signature is the hand-written dispatch table — when V5-080 replaces it with generated code, this signature stops matching and the entry is re-reviewed rather than silently outliving its own removal plan.

entries.structuralReason: Build output, not source. Coverage is measured on src/** before tsdown emits it.
entries.justification: Generated artifacts carry no independent test surface.
